newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil spill pollutes farm, river.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil spill pollutes farm, river.

text.p: Two oil spills have hit the Egbema community in eastern Nigeria, polluting farmland and and a river, witnesses said on Wednesday.
They said they were caused by leakages in pipelines belonging to the local units of Royal/Dutch Shell Group and Agip SpA.
The spills occurred a fortnight ago, they added.
An official report had been lodged in Owerri with the Imo state government, which was investigating the matter, officials of the state government said.
Shell and Agip officials were not available to comment because of a public holiday in Lagos in honour of Nigeria's first president Nnamdi Azikiwe who died in May and is to be buried this weekend.
Oil spillages are common in Nigeria where multinational oil companies accuse local people of damaging their pipelines in order to claim compensation.
Local communities in turn accuse the companies of failing to replace ageing flowlines and pipelines which they say are responsible for the leaks.
